questions.question: If two cars are traveling the same 10-mile distance, how does the speed of the faster car affect its travel time compared to the slower car?
options: The faster car takes less time to cover the distance.
The faster car takes more time to cover the distance.
Both cars take the same amount of time.
The faster car's time depends only on its mass.

questions.question: Two cyclists ride for exactly 30 minutes. Cyclist A has a higher speed than Cyclist B. What does this mean for the distance travelled?
options: Cyclist A travels less distance than Cyclist B.
Cyclist A travels a greater distance than Cyclist B.
Both cyclists travel the exact same distance.
Cyclist B travels twice the distance of Cyclist A.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct formula used to calculate speed?
options: Speed = distance × time
Speed = time ÷ distance
Speed = distance ÷ time
Speed = distance + time

questions.question: What is the effect of a non-zero resultant force acting on a moving object?
options: It must change the mass of the object.
It can change the speed of the object.
It will always keep the speed perfectly constant.
It has no effect on the motion of the object.

questions.question: On a distance-time graph, what does a steeper line (greater gradient) represent?
options: The object is moving faster.
The object is moving slower.
The object has stopped moving.
The object is moving backwards at a constant slow speed.

questions.question: When does a falling object reach its terminal velocity?
options: When the drag force is zero.
When gravity stops pulling on the object.
When the drag force and gravitational force are equal.
When the drag force is twice the gravitational force.

questions.question: How does opening a parachute change the terminal velocity of a skydiver?
options: It decreases the gravitational pull, speeding up the fall.
It changes the terminal velocity by increasing the drag force.
It increases terminal velocity by reducing air resistance.
It has no effect on the terminal velocity of the skydiver.

questions.question: What is the relationship between the surface area of a parachute and its drag force?
options: A larger surface area produces a smaller drag force.
A larger surface area produces a bigger drag force.
Changing the surface area does not affect the drag force.
A larger surface area only increases drag when gravity increases.

questions.question: When a skydiver with a parachute is falling at a constant top speed, how does the drag force compare to the force of gravity on the jumper?
options: The drag force is much larger than the force of gravity.
The drag force is smaller than the force of gravity.
The drag force is the same size as the force of gravity.
The drag force is zero.

questions.question: What does a horizontal, level line on a distance-time graph indicate about an object's motion?
options: The object is moving at a high constant speed.
The object is stationary and not moving.
The object is accelerating rapidly.
The object is returning to its starting position.

questions.question: If an upward sloping line on a distance-time graph represents a person walking away from home, what does a downward sloping line represent?
options: The person is walking in the opposite direction (towards home).
The person is standing still.
The person is walking away from home at a faster speed.
The person is climbing a steep hill.

questions.question: Why do scientists take repeat readings during timing experiments?
options: To eliminate systematic errors completely.
To reduce the effect of random errors.
To increase the total time taken for the experiment.
To make sure the object moves faster.

questions.question: In which direction does friction act on a sliding block?
options: In the same direction as the block's movement.
Upwards, perpendicular to the surface.
Against the direction of the block's movement.
Downwards, towards the center of the Earth.

questions.question: What happens to a moving object if there is no resultant force acting on it?
options: It will gradually slow down and eventually stop.
It will continue to move at a steady speed in a straight line.
It will instantly speed up to its maximum limit.
It will begin to move in a circular path.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of streamlining the shape of a high-speed train?
options: To increase the gravitational force acting on it.
To reduce drag.
To increase the friction between the wheels and track.
To make the train heavier.

questions.question: How does the drag force on an object moving through water change as its speed increases?
options: The drag force decreases.
The drag force remains constant.
The drag force increases.
The drag force drops to zero.
